title: Vulnerability Triage Sprint Summary (dry run) - 2026-12-14
content:
Meeting: Security Engineering sync — vulnerability triage sprint dry run
Date: 2026-12-14 10:00–11:15 PT
Location: Zoom / #sec-triage
Facilitator: Nora Chen
Attendees: Nora Chen, Samir Rao, Elena Martinez, Jonah Park, Priya Kulkarni, Riley Adams (notes)

TL;DR:
- Dry-run triage of the 'quarterly sprint' process completed. We reviewed 18 active findings surfaced over the past 3 weeks (internal scanners + 3rd-party intel).
- Outcome: 3 items classified as High, 6 Medium, 9 Low. Confirmed ticket ownership, immediate mitigations for the 3 Highs, and a rollout plan for improved secrets scanning rules.
- Decisions: start a 2-week canary of automated secret rotation (namespace-limited), tighten S3 presigned URL caching rules, and add File Upload Service to the threat-model backlog.

Goals for this session:
- Validate triage rubric and sprint cadence (time-to-fix / SLA targets).
- Assign owners and immediate mitigations for highest-risk items.
- Exercise cross-team escalation (infra, platform, product).

Summary of triaged findings:
- Total reviewed: 18 (source: internal-scan-2026-11-29, burp-reports-3rdparty-2026-12-03, dependency-scan-2026-12-01).
- High (3):
  1) H1: Long-lived API tokens discovered in the ingestion service logs snapshot. Evidence: archived logs contained full bearer tokens from an older connector. Immediate risk: token replay/exfiltration. (Action: rotate tokens, remove sensitive logs). Ticket: SEC-4821.
  2) H2: Kubernetes role binding overly permissive in canary cluster allowing pod exec on worker nodes. Evidence from auditd logs. Immediate risk: lateral movement. (Action: rollback patch, apply least-privilege RBAC policy). Ticket: SEC-4910.
  3) H3: S3 presigned URL with infinite cache control header cached by CDN edge for >30d in one customer-facing endpoint (file hosting). Immediate risk: prolonged access to signed content after intended expiry. (Action: set cache-control, short TTL, reissue URLs, add integration test). Ticket: SEC-4942 (created during meeting).
- Medium (6): stale third-party dependency with recent CVE (fasttext-like package flagged for deserialization vulnerability), misconfigured VPC peering route exposing internal metadata endpoints to a partner account, insecure CORS wildcard on analytics ingest, and three medium misconfigs in CI secrets handling (see list in content).
- Low (9): informational findings and dev ergonomics issues (unused service accounts, expired test certs, a couple of non-privileged tokens in archived test fixtures).

Threat modeling items discussed:
- File Upload Service: new mini-threat-model added to backlog. Risk vectors called out: zipbomb/resource exhaustion, malicious wasm execution (we run wasm in a sandboxed runner), content-type mismatch leading to server-side template rendering, and metadata exfil via user-provided callback URL. Proposed mitigations: content-size limits, asynchronous virus/behavior scanning, strict content-type enforcement, disallow direct user callbacks without verification. Owner: Elena Martinez. Confluence stub created for the model: (internal link in linked_artifacts).

Secrets inventory and scanning update:
- Inventory snapshot: 92 managed secrets across envs; 12 secrets flagged stale/unused; 4 secrets in the 'at-risk' bucket because they appear in logs or archived artifacts.
- Action approved: run a dry-run of automated rotation for non-production namespaces (two-week canary). Scope: 3 services (ingestion, data-mover, model-cache). Rotation automation component: infrasec/secrets-rotator (PR linked).
- Rollout plan for scanner rules: tighten regex for presigned URLs, add rule to detect cache-control headers in responses, add rule to detect long-lived tokens in logs. Jonah to update scanner ruleset and open PR.

Escalation and on-call coordination:
- For any confirmed H1/H2 incidents, PagerDuty runbook 'sec-high-vuln' is in effect (escalation to SecEng lead, infra SRE, and assigned service owner).
- Reminder: when a vulnerability requires rotation of customer-facing keys, coordinate with CS and product for customer notifications. Priya to draft a notification template for rotations impacting customers.

Decisions and rationale:
- Start a 2-week canary of automated rotation in dev-staging only. Rationale: verify rollout behavior and detect breakage without impacting production traffic.
- Require CDN cache-control header enforcement for any presigned URL path. Rationale: prevents prolonged exposure even if URL leaks.
- Promote RBAC policy changes to canary cluster first and validate via chaos tests (pod-impersonation tests).

Concrete action items (owner, due):
- Nora: create high-priority incident ticket SEC-4942 for presigned URL TTL fix; due 2026-12-15.
- Jonah: update scanner rules (presigned URL, log-token detection) and open PR; due 2026-12-17. Linked: github PR referenced.
- Elena: draft File Upload Service threat model and attack matrix; due 2026-12-21.
- Samir: implement canary rotation pipeline for ingestion/data-mover/model-cache (dev-staging only) and run smoke tests; due 2026-12-22.
- Priya: customer notification template for key rotations + runbook for CS; due 2026-12-18.
- Riley: coordinate RBAC rollback playbook and validate in canary cluster; due 2026-12-16.
- All: confirm owners for Medium items in SEC backlog by end of sprint planning meeting (2026-12-18).

Risk and blocking items:
- Dependency CVE required coordinated upgrade; we need approval for a minor version bump that touches model-serving packaging. Blocked by release window; engineering to advise on compatible patch.
- Secrets rotation automation depends on one infra API rate-limit increase (support ticket open with infra team). Without the rate-limit change, rotation will take >48h for full scope — unacceptable for rapid remediation.

Notes from the dry-run retrospection (process-level feedback):
- Good: faster owner assignment, clear SLA targets established (24h acknowledge for High, 72h mitigation window where possible).
- Needs improvement: runbook linking inside tickets — make runbook checklist a required field on all High tickets.
- Suggestion: add an 'impact matrix' quick reference to triage docs that maps service criticality × exploitability -> recommended time-to-fix. Samir to prototype.

Open questions for leadership:
- Do we want automated customer notification for key rotations that are non-security-critical? (tradeoff: noise vs transparency).
- Can infra provision a temporary higher API quota for secrets-rotation canary? (blocking item)

Appendix: quick list of ticket refs created/updated in meeting:
- SEC-4821 (ingestion token rotation) — owner Samir — updated during meeting
- SEC-4910 (canary RBAC rollback) — owner Riley — ready for canary validation
- SEC-4942 (presigned URL TTL enforcement) — Nora — created in meeting
- DEP-2034 (dependency CVE analysis) — engineering lead TODO to accept patch

Next steps / next sync:
- Follow-up sync scheduled: 2026-12-21 10:00 PT (focus: canary progress & medium-item reassignment)
- Pre-sync checklist: updated scanner PR, canary pipeline logs accessible, draft notification template available.

Raw notes / fragments captured during triage (copied verbatim where helpful):
- "Found bearer token in archived logs — probably from connector alpha that hadn't redacted logs after migration"
- "CDN cached presigned URL — edge set to respect origin cache-control but origin misconfigured"
- "fasttext-like dep flagged; likely safe after patch but we need to validate model-serialization path"

End of notes.
If you're an assignee and haven't been pinged directly, please add yourself to the ticket and comment with a short mitigation plan by EOD 2026-12-15.
